agent_review.author: agent

findings.summary: The prepared clone ended in whiteout after 23 verified actions.
findings.observed_fact: Snackodile was reduced from 2 HP to 0 by Lopunny Drain Punch; no usable Pokémon remained and the cartridge reported GPT whited out.
findings.strategic_judgment: The action bundle did not preserve a survivable line and must not qualify or retry unchanged.
findings.next_test: Correct preparation and no-safe-line handling, then run a fresh disposable clone from the protected opening.
findings.state_unavailable_reason: The terminal whiteout state is not a reversible pre-decision fixture; causal decision states are attached to the preparation and policy findings.

findings.summary: The current six-Pokémon build had no verified safe continuation after the opening switch into Kubfu.
findings.observed_fact: The opening switch to Lildozer was safe, but the next selected Bulldoze and Ice Shard decisions were both unsafe; Lildozer then fainted before Kubfu was defeated.
findings.strategic_judgment: Readiness accepted a team whose first matchup could not sustain a verified follow-up. Preparation must prove survivability and reserve depth, not only full HP and legal moves.
findings.next_test: Recompute owned-counter/build options and validate a replacement team or move/order plan against exact Brawly damage and reserve constraints.

findings.summary: The policy selected unsafe actions instead of stopping the clone for preparation.

resolution.observed: Exact disposable replay stopped before input with no safe legal action; corrected clone gate preserved state a5e4bd76e5820016.

findings.observed_fact: At turn 2 the selected Bulldoze had safe=false and survival margin -10; at turn 3 the selected Ice Shard had safe=false and survival margin -35, with no safe continuation reported.
findings.strategic_judgment: When every legal line is unsafe, continuing damage-only actions spends a clone and hides a preparation failure. The hard-fight runner needs a deterministic no-safe-line gate.
findings.next_test: Replay turn 2 after adding the gate and require a verified preparation stop rather than an unsafe input.

findings.summary: Fresh-entry Fake Out was treated as safe without modeling Lopunny’s Eject Button replacement.

resolution.observed: Exact disposable replay at the attached Lopunny state forbade the nonlethal Eject Button-triggering Fake Out and stopped before input at 8482689ea16c3897.

findings.observed_fact: The selected Fake Out certificate listed fresh_entry_flinch and safe=true while recording defender_held_item_effect_unmodeled:501; the cartridge then forced Lopunny out with Eject Button and sent Combusken.
findings.strategic_judgment: The fresh Fake Out rule is valid only when the forced replacement risk is modeled. Item-triggered replacement can invalidate the apparent free turn and must affect ranking or uncertainty.
findings.next_test: Add deterministic Eject Button replacement handling and replay the attached turn-9 state; Fake Out must no longer receive an unqualified safe bonus.

findings.summary: After the Eject Button replacement, the policy continued with two known-unsafe attacks and lost Croakatoa.

resolution.observed: Exact disposable replay at the attached Combusken state stopped before input because no safe legal action existed; Mud Shot and Vacuum Wave were not executed.

findings.observed_fact: Mud Shot and Vacuum Wave were selected with safe=false and survival margins -36 and -78; Croakatoa fainted while Combusken remained alive.
findings.strategic_judgment: The scorer exposed a second active to a known losing exchange instead of refusing the line or preserving the reserve for a prepared replay.
findings.next_test: Replay turn 10 with the corrected no-safe-line and replacement-risk logic and verify that no unsafe attack is executed.

findings.summary: Ohmnomnom was kept in through a deteriorating Lopunny exchange without a verified preservation line.
findings.observed_fact: Spark was used four times; Ohmnomnom fell from 59 HP to 31, then 3, then fainted while Lopunny survived at 12 HP.
findings.strategic_judgment: This is a reusable reserve-preservation candidate, but no switch or Fake Out alternative has yet been bounded-replayed as lexicographically dominant because the recorded switches were unsafe.
findings.next_test: Bound one fresh-entry Fake Out and one preservation switch from turn 13 before changing the ranking.

findings.summary: The tail of the fight spent six actions on damage-only exchanges after all active choices were unsafe.
findings.observed_fact: Coppertop used Rock Smash twice and Snackodile used Bulldoze three times into Lopunny Drain Punch; the sequence ended in whiteout without a safe candidate.
findings.strategic_judgment: The repeated tail added frames, PP use, and exposure without improving the verified outcome; the new gate should stop at the earliest no-safe state.
findings.next_test: Confirm the corrected runner stops once the safe candidate set is empty and records the exact stop state.

findings.summary: The failed clone consumed Fake Out, Spark, Rock Smash, and Bulldoze PP without a win.
findings.observed_fact: The clone spent one Fake Out, four Spark, two Rock Smash, and four Bulldoze uses before whiteout.
findings.strategic_judgment: This is secondary to survival, but a no-safe-line stop and better preparation will preserve resources for the next verified attempt.
findings.next_test: Measure PP and action count on the corrected clone before qualification.

correct_choices: The clone began from the protected opening and every submitted action was verified against the cartridge.
The initial Croakatoa-to-Lildozer switch was safe against Kubfu and preserved Croakatoa.
Bushtank safely removed Kubfu after the forced replacement and all forced switches were obeyed.
The runner did not touch the authoritative live emulator during the disposable loss.
agent_review.next_test: Fix the shared Eject Button mechanics and clone no-safe-line gate, recompute the prepared team, resolve every attached high-severity finding by exact replay, then start clone 1 again.
